title: Discrete time liquids
authors: Zuo Wang, Paul M. Schindler, Marin Bukov, Marios H. Michael
abstract: Discrete time crystals exhibit robust subharmonic oscillations, spontaneously breaking the discrete time-translation symmetry of a periodic drive. Since their emergence, the question of whether other types of temporal many-body order can exist has attracted considerable attention. Here we identify discrete time liquids -- a new form of spatiotemporal order characterized by short-range temporal coherence as a result of time-solitons. We study a two-dimensional spin system coupled to a finite-temperature cavity, whose fluctuations provide a noisy, approximately periodic drive with only finite temporal coherence. Remarkably, the spins nevertheless form a metastable state with robust period-doubled dynamics over an extended parameter regime. Unlike a time crystal, this state has only finite temporal coherence: individual trajectories stochastically switch between the two symmetry-related temporal configurations of the period-doubled response. We identify these switches as time-solitons: topological defects in temporal order that preserve local period doubling while destroying long-range temporal coherence, thereby producing the time liquid state. We propose a minimal model which reproduces the distribution of temporal correlations of the many-body system, suggesting a general description of the time liquid as a time crystal with a finite density of time-solitons. Because these solitons can occur at arbitrary times, ensemble averaging restores continuous time-translation symmetry, raising the intriguing possibility that discrete time liquids can exist in thermal equilibrium.
summary: This paper introduces the concept of a Discrete Time Liquid (DTL), a novel form of temporal order distinct from time crystals. It models a spin system driven by the thermal fluctuations of a cavity, showing that robust period-doubling can occur even when the drive is noisy and short-lived. The key mechanism involves topological defects called time-solitons, which destroy long-range coherence but stabilize the local period-doubled state.
main_problem: The paper investigates temporal many-body order beyond conventional time crystals, specifically focusing on order induced by noisy, finite-coherence external drives.
main_result: The authors identify a new state called the Discrete Time Liquid (DTL), characterized by local period-doubling dynamics but lacking long-range temporal coherence due to time-solitons.
method: The study uses theoretical modeling, analyzing the system's response to an effective, noisy drive generated by a coupled cavity mode, and proposing a minimal stochastic-switching model.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional spin lattice coupled to a finite-temperature cavity mode. The dynamics are governed by a spin Hamiltonian coupled to the cavity's Langevin equation, creating an effective, noisy drive.
key_observables: Temporal order (period-doubling), temporal coherence, and the density of time-solitons.
important_parameters: Bath temperature ($T_{	ext{bath}}$), cavity coherence time ($	au_{	ext{cav}}$), and the ratio of correlation times ($\langle\langle	au_{corr}angleangle/	au_{th}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis treats spins classically and relies on the effective drive generated by the cavity fluctuations, which is assumed to generate a Rayleigh distribution at high temperatures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition between free precession, time crystal, and time liquid regimes based on bath temperature, showing period doubling induced by thermal noise. Phase diagrams map out the system's behavior using multiple timescales.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the physical model (spin-cavity coupling), demonstrating the emergence of period doubling under noisy drives, identifying the time-soliton mechanism responsible for finite coherence, and finally proposing the DTL state and its implications for thermal equilibrium.
why_interesting: This work bridges the concepts of time crystals and liquid states in non-equilibrium systems, providing a mechanism (time-solitons) to sustain robust temporal order even when the driving field lacks long-range coherence, which is highly relevant for understanding driven quantum matter.
